attempted_claim: Let Y be a compact, orientable, irreducible hyperbolic 3-manifold with one incompressible torus boundary, H_1(Y; Q) ≅ Q, and more than one L-space Dehn filling (so Y is Floer simple). For every non-longitudinal rational slope α on ∂Y, is π_1(Y(α)) non-left-orderable if and only if α belongs to L(Y) = {β : Y(β) is an L-space}?
decisive_failure: The investigation could not close either implication of the conjectured equivalence: hyperbolic L-space fillings admit no citable Heegaard Floer to left-orderability obstruction, and non-L-space fillings admit no uniform left-orderability construction, with existing foliation and order-detection theorems covering only slopes near the longitude.
